title: Harmonize slab-surface variables and compact typography for dense tables & action bars
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Legacy token sets drift across tables, buttons, and compact action bars resulting in inconsistent surface depth, contrast, and cramped typography at high data densities. Goal: introduce a small set of variable slab-surface tokens (color + micro-elevation), a proportional radius scale tied to the spacing system, and a compact typography scale for dense tables and row actions. This work must preserve accessibility (AA for body, AA/AAA where possible for interactive labels), be backwards-compatible via a migration adapter, and be rollout-safe (canary + opt-out).

Scope:
- Define 6 new surface slab tokens (slab-0..slab-5) with color and elevation deltas for card/list/table backgrounds.
- Define a proportional radius token series (r-slab-1..r-slab-4) computed as fractions of the base spacing token to ensure rhythm.
- Compact typography scale: body-compact, label-compact, caption-compact with line-height and tracking deltas for legibility in dense rows.
- Micro-elevation / shadow ramp: 3-step penumbra optimized for small corner radii and subpixel rendering.
- Migration adapter: CSS var aliases + per-component delta map so customers can opt-in or pin legacy tokens.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Trade-off between perceived depth and rendering performance: stronger shadows increase GPU compositing; we choose low-contrast, offset-only shadows with a subtle blur to reduce overdraw while keeping depth cues.
- Radius proportionality vs fixed pixel radii: proportional radii scale better across density modes but can change visual weight in legacy layouts; we include a per-component override map.
- Contrast: some compact label states push token contrast close to AA; we've chosen color adjustments on slab-1 and slab-2 to preserve text legibility in dark and light modes.

Acceptance criteria (see separate list field): includes token spec, figma redlines, integration PR, and visual regression tolerances.

Cross-functional reviewers: PM (Ben Ortega), Engineering owners (Runtime UI: Sienna Park), Accessibility lead (Dr. Oliver Ng).
updates: 2026-03-05: Discovery workshop completed; inventory of 42 affected components (tables, row-actions, toolbar, bulk-select) documented in Confluence.
2026-03-07: Prototype in Figma for dense table rows + compact typography created (v1) — initial feedback calls out button hit area risk in compact mode.
2026-03-09: Engineering spike started to test micro-elevation rendering perf on Safari & Chromium — initial results: minor repaint cost with box-shadow, better with layered pseudo-elements.
2026-03-11: Decided to use offset-only shadows + alpha-tuned color to reduce composition cost; added per-component override plan to address hit-area concerns.
2026-03-13: PR opened for token definitions and migration aliases (github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/428); QA smoke tests scheduled.
2026-03-14: Design review (Sienna, Ben, Oliver) — approved visual direction pending final contrast tests and release gating notes.
acceptance_criteria: Token spec published: color swatches, alpha values, elevation offsets, and CSS var names (slab-0..slab-5, r-slab-1..r-slab-4)
Figma redlines and component variants updated for tables, row actions, bulk toolbar, and compact buttons
Migration adapter implemented with aliases; customers can toggle new tokens via CSS root class
No visual-regression failures beyond agreed tolerances in the screenshot suite for critical pages
Accessibility: body text maintains AA contrast in both light/dark modes; interactive labels meet AA when in compact mode where feasible
Performance: local render perf tests do not increase main-thread time by >5% on supported browsers
notes: Implementation path: land token definitions first, then component-level deltas in a follow-up PR to reduce blast radius.
Consider adding an automatic telemetry flag to detect layout breakage after rollout to 5% of accounts.
We should register a short runway for mobile grid differences — proportional radii require a special case at very small viewports.
Follow-up work: craft migration docs for partners using on-prem templates (Private customers) to avoid surprise visual shifts.
